newsitem.title: CHINA: Hang Seng Bank H1 net at high end of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank H1 net at high end of forecasts.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd posted a 14.5 percent rise in interim net profit on Monday, at the high end of analysts' expectations, with strong loan growth and an improvement in provisions for bad and doubtful debt.

The bank said profit attributable to shareholders rose to HK$4.98 billion during the first six months of 1997 compared with HK$4.35 billion in the same 1996 period. Analysts had expected net profit growth of between 11 and 15 percent.
Operating profit rose 13.7 percent to HK$5.10 billion.

"The operating result benefited from the satisfactory growth in both net interest income and other operating income, a lean cost structure, and an improvement in provisions for bad and doubtful debts," the company said in a statement.
Net interest income rose to HK$5.50 billion compared with HK$5.01 billion in the first half of 1996. Average interest earnings assets rose 11.6 percent to HK$360.41 billion.
"The results benefited from the strong growth in advances to customers and an increased proportion of current and savings accounts," Hang Seng Bank said.
Advances to customers, net of provisions, rose 18.2 percent since the end of 1996 to HK$194.48 billion.
"There was strong growth in corporate lending and residential mortgages," Hang Seng Bank said.
The net charge for bad and doubtful debts fell by HK$15 million compared with the first half of 1996 to HK$205 million.

"This was the result of a substantial reduction in specific provisions, offset by the much higher general provisions made in line with the strong loan growth in the first half of 1997," Hang Seng Bank said.

But it said it had suffered from a fall in residential mortgage pricing, due to fierce competition. Hang Seng Bank's net interest margin for the first half of the year fell to 3.08 percent from 3.12 percent during the same period last year.
Hang Seng Bank said it registered a 13.0 percent rise in net fees and commissions receivable to HK$817 million and dealing profits grew 5.0 percent to HK$251 million.
"There was strong growth in net fees and commissions from broking, card and account services, although a marginal decline was recorded in fee income from credit facilities," Hang Seng Bank said.
Profit on the disposal of tangible fixed assets and investment securities rose by HK$84 million to HK$602 million.
"This was mainly due to the increase in profit on disposal of locally listed equities," Hang Seng Bank said.
Operating expenses rose 3.8 percent to HK$1.77 billion.
The cost income ratio improved to 25.0 percent from 26.6 percent in the first half of 1996.
